_notes: game_state added locally from a 4-player game on an ALP4K cabinet.
Scores are 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x02110A9C: that game ended 2,280,980 / 805,550 /
1,226,760 / 991,480 and those landed there. Not the base twd_156c uses, which is 0x021109E4 on a
4-byte stride -- the same title at another revision, and another reminder that the score layout is
per-ROM on SAM.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent bytes in CPU RAM at 0x00036134 and 0x00036135, player
low and ball high, the shape every SAM game checked so far uses. The player byte completed 1->2->3
three times, once per ball, against one completion for the ball.
player_count at 0x02110900, the one address shared across all of them.
game_over, tilted, credits and volume come from a 974-frame recording of live memory spanning
an operator-menu session and one five-ball game with a mid-ball tilt on ball 1. The menu session
also promoted ball_count and max_credits from derived to measured: Balls Per Game 3 -> 5 landed
at adjustment index 32 and Max Credits 30 -> 9 at index 34, three and one records below the
free play record at index 35, as the free_play-relative rule predicted.
0x00036166 is the status bitfield SAM games keep at ball+0x31: 1 in attract, 41 at each ball
start, 20 in play, 22 for exactly the ten samples between the tilt and the end of the tilted
ball, during which player 1's score sat frozen at 191,060. 41 and 20 share no bit, so game_over
is 'any bit above 0x01' -- mask 0xFE inverted -- correct in all 974 frames. tilted is bit 0x02,
which no non-tilt value carries on this game.
volume at 0x02110204 -- not the 0x02110250 used by twd_156 -- moving 59, 60, 58 in the operator
menu with its complement check byte following; declared as checksum8. credits at 0x0211100C,
the nineteenth SAM game at that address, stepping down at game start and up again at the end
of the game when the match awarded a credit.
Adjustment index 39, four records above free play, is Ball Save Timer (5 -> 0 in the same
menu session); not a mapped field.
bytes have read zero in every image captured, so the width is taken from the record's
The record is 36 bytes with the checksum at +32, so four bytes sit between the 4-byte score at
+24 and the checksum. They read zero in every image captured (163 records across five games)
and their purpose is not established: they are consistent with the upper half of a 64-bit score,
but this game's champion-threshold table at 0x021024F8 stores its thresholds as 4-byte values
with a complement check byte, which is what a 32-bit score would be compared against. The score
is therefore declared as 4 bytes until a value above 2^32 is observed or the ROM is disassembled.
2026-11: The A.1 (64) and A.2 (169) adjustments added from the ROM image (README, 'Adjustments
from the ROM').
Confirmed on a cabinet 2026-11-13 (ALP4K; two players, tilt on P1 ball 1): 1,122,950 /
2,508,130, the records and the status byte matched the DMD (29 at each ball served).
